html:
The Kulina Pano are a small Panoan people of the Javari River valley in western Amazonas, Brazil, near the border with Peru. Today most live in the village of Pedro Lopes on the middle Curuçá River, inside the Vale do Javari Indigenous Land.

Their language, with the dialects Kapishtana, Mawi and Chema, is no longer in daily use, and everyone also speaks Portuguese. They should not be confused with the Kulina (Madija), whose language is Arawan. Their Panoan neighbours include the Marubo and the Matsés.
